request.spec:
A steward can roll the year over: a year entry and a button. It generates the next fiscal year's
twelve periods exactly as the fiscal year generator does, and for each person their open figure at
the end of the old year's last period (the due of their claims that count, belonging to a period of
the old year, OPEN or PENDING at that period's end) is added to their carried figure for the new
year's first period as OPENING_SET lines; then ROLLOVER fy=<old FY> periods=<made> is written. A year
with no periods, anyone but a steward, or a bad year is refused with an error.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can roll the year over: a year entry and a button. It generates the next fiscal year's
twelve periods exactly as the fiscal year generator does, and for each person their open figure at
the end of the old year's last period (the due of their claims that count, belonging to a period of
the old year, OPEN or PENDING at that period's end) is added to their carried figure for the new
year's first period as OPENING_SET lines; then ROLLOVER fy=<old FY> periods=<made> is written. A year
with no periods, anyone but a steward, or a bad year is refused with an error.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the rollover. Three of the four tests in `bin/e2e` pass, including the main rollover test with its full audit check. "Year end rollover scenario 2" still fails, at a check that has nothing to do with rollover. I didn't change anything to make it pass.

**What I added**
- **Server:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/rollover` endpoint (`rollover.POST.yml`), handled by the new `period/RolloverFiscalYear.java`. Viewers are blocked first, and the year is checked by the same rule the fiscal year generator uses. Then it:
  - refuses anyone who isn't a steward, and refuses a year with no periods on the sheet;
  - makes the next fiscal year's twelve periods with the generator's own code, which writes the `PERIOD_ADDED` lines;
  - works out each person's open figure for the old year and adds it to their opening balance for the new year's first period, writing an `OPENING_SET` line for each;
  - finally writes `ROLLOVER fy=FY<old> periods=<made>` and returns how many periods it made.
- **Screen:** a "Roll over FY" year box and button in the periods section (`features/periods/periods.slot.tsx`). It shows how many periods were made, or an error; the error clears when you edit the year or press the button again.

**Choices the request didn't settle**
- A person whose open figure is 0.00 gets no `OPENING_SET` line.
- If the new year's periods can't be made (because they overlap existing periods) and none exist already, there is no first period to carry figures into. In that case it carries nothing and still writes `ROLLOVER … periods=0`.

**Why scenario 2 fails** (line 1528 of the spec: `rate-month-C-2026-04` should be `12.50` but shows `n/a`)
- That test views the sheet as of 2026-03-20, and the `12.50` it expects is a rate inherited from a parent sheet.
- The test never sets the parent sheet's date, so it takes the real date (2026-11-11). That makes the parent's rates look set after 2026-03-20, so the as-of view leaves them out.
- So the expected value only appears if the test runs on or before 2026-03-20. It depends on the real date, not on this change. Making it pass would mean changing how the existing as-of rate view works, which this change shouldn't do.
